title: verification_plan.v1
description: The product's verification plan (SWE.4 BP1, BP2): one section per verification level. Stored as one fenced ```yaml verification_plan block in qf.yaml paths.verification_plan_file, written by the tester before the first unit test and agreed at the pull request. The unit section is written at stage 5; the integration section by the assembler at stage 7 (SWE.5 BP1, BP3), required by check_verification_plan_gate once the product has integration tests; the software section by the bridge tester at stage 8 (SWE.6 BP1, BP2), required once the product has software-level tests; the validation section by the crew that writes the validation scenarios at stage 11 (VAL.1 BP1, BP2), required once the product has a scenario. Each section holds the commands that run its level's suites (suites), each naming its tool, a test_runner row of the stack (UNKNOWN_TOOL), which gives the version. That every suite a requirement names has a command once its level's section exists (UNKNOWN_INSTRUMENT) is a rule of check_verification_plan_gate; that the measured coverage reaches the minimum, of check_stack_commands_gate.

techniques.description: How unit tests are derived, e.g. one test per acceptance criterion, boundary values at every range limit.

pass_fail_criteria.description: When a unit test run passes, and what a failure blocks.

entry_criteria.description: What must hold before unit verification starts.

exit_criteria.description: What must hold for unit verification to be done.

infrastructure.description: The test runner, test doubles and other tools needed.

selection.description: Which unit tests run, and when (SWE.4 BP2).

regression.description: Which existing unit tests run again when code changes (SWE.4 BP2).

time_budget.description: How long the unit tests may take on CI (decision 33 of the unit stages); without it the framework's defaults apply: the suite 120 seconds, each test 0.5 seconds.

coverage.description: The minimum code coverage the unit tests must reach (SWE.4 BP2).

suites.description: The command that runs the unit tests; it also measures coverage.

integration.description: Component and integration verification (SWE.5 BP1–BP3). That the order names existing components, each component in some step, is a rule of check_verification_plan_gate; that each step's selection has a passing test, of verify_tests_to_components_link_gate.

techniques.description: How component and integration tests are derived, e.g. one test per flow of the approved sequence diagrams.

infrastructure.description: What the tests need, e.g. a test database in a container, a stub for an external service.

regression.description: Which component and integration tests run again when a component changes (SWE.5 BP3).

time_budget.description: How long the integration suite may take on CI (decision 33 of the unit stages); without it the framework's default applies: 300 seconds.

order.description: The integration order (SWE.5 BP1): the steps in which the components are integrated.

components.description: The components integrated in this step.

preconditions.description: What must be true before the step, e.g. database migrated.

selection.description: The flows and components whose tests run after this step (SWE.5 BP3).

suites.description: The command that runs the component and integration tests.

software.description: Software verification (SWE.6 BP1, BP2): the integrated software against every requirement of both levels.

techniques.description: How software-level tests are derived, e.g. one test per acceptance criterion, a benchmark per performance requirement.

infrastructure.description: The environment the integrated software runs in, e.g. deployed in a test environment with sample data.

selection.description: Which software-level tests run, and when (SWE.6 BP2).

regression.description: Which software-level tests run again after a change (SWE.6 BP2).

time_budget.description: How long the software suite may take on CI (decision 33 of the unit stages); without it the framework's default applies: 600 seconds.

order.description: The order in which the suites run (SWE.6 BP1), from the suite vocabulary.

suites.description: The commands that run the software-level suites a requirement can name: software, e2e, bench, security.

validation.description: Validation (VAL.1 BP1, BP2): the product against the customer's wishes, in conditions close to the customer's. That every scenario is listed and every listed scenario exists is a rule of check_verification_plan_gate.

selection.description: Which scenarios run before each release (VAL.1 BP2): every automated one, and which of those run by hand.

regression.description: Which scenarios run again after a change, e.g. every scenario of a wish the release touches (VAL.1 BP2).

scenarios.description: Every scenario, in the order they run (VAL.1 BP1).

scenario.description: The scenario's repository path, under qf.yaml paths.validation_scenarios_dir.

technique.description: e.g. acceptance test, guided demo, trial use.

pass_fail_criteria.description: When the customer counts the scenario as passed, in their terms.

entry_criteria.description: What must hold before it runs, e.g. the release deployed to staging with realistic data.

environment.description: Where it runs: conditions close to the customer's, e.g. staging with realistic data and the same integrations.

suites.description: The command that runs the automated validation scenarios against the deployed release; absent when every scenario is run by a person.

suite_seconds.description: The longest the full suite may run, in wall-clock seconds.

reason.description: Why the budget is looser than the framework's default; required then (check_time_budget_gate).

suite_seconds.description: The longest the full unit suite may run, in wall-clock seconds.

test_seconds.description: The longest one unit test may take, in seconds, as its JUnit result records it.

reason.description: Why the budget is looser than the framework's default; required then (check_time_budget_gate).

report.description: Repository-relative path or glob of a file a suite writes; a glob for tools that write one file per test class (e.g. target/surefire-reports/TEST-*.xml).

tool.description: The tool that runs the suite: the name of a test_runner row of the stack, which gives its version and version command.

results.description: Where the suite writes its test results, as JUnit XML.

coverage.description: Where the suite writes its code coverage, as Cobertura XML.

measurements.description: Where the suite writes the values it measures, as measurements.v1 JSON (SWE.6 BP3).

run_selected.description: The command that runs only the given tests (decision 31 of the unit stages): run with {tests} in place of the selected tests, written as selected_form says. A suite without it runs in full on every change.

selected_form.description: How {tests} lists the selected tests: paths — their files, relative to the product root, separated by spaces; names — their file names without extension, separated by commas (e.g. LoginTest,LockoutTest).

test_files.description: Glob patterns of the suite's test files, relative to the folder its level's tests live in: paths.code_dir for unit (they tell a test file from code, e.g. **/*Test.java), paths.integration_tests_dir, paths.software_tests_dir, paths.validation_scenarios_dir (a scenario matching none is run by a person).

unit_suite.description: The unit suite also measures coverage: SWE.4 BP2 compares it with the minimum of the coverage section.
